title: Search Algorithms and Data Structures

topics.name: Hash Tables
topics.description: A hash table uses a hash function to map keys to array indices enabling O(1) average-case lookup. Collisions are resolved by chaining or open addressing. Hash tables underpin inverted indexes in search engines for fast term lookup.

topics.name: Binary Search Trees
topics.description: A binary search tree stores elements in sorted order allowing O(log n) search insert and delete operations. Balanced variants like AVL trees and Red-Black trees guarantee worst-case O(log n) performance.

topics.name: Trie
topics.description: A trie also called prefix tree is a tree data structure for storing strings. Each node represents a character prefix. Tries are used in autocomplete systems and spell checkers in search engines.

topics.name: Skip Lists
topics.description: A skip list is a probabilistic data structure that allows O(log n) search within an ordered sequence. It is used in some IR systems like Apache Lucene for storing postings lists efficiently.

applications: These data structures are fundamental to building efficient inverted indexes, query processors, and ranking systems in information retrieval.
